result.summary: The image shows a mixed-use urban intersection with a marked continental crosswalk and basic traffic signals. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the environment lacks pedestrian-specific signals and features significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles near the crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the main roadway approaching the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is signalized for vehicles but lacks dedicated walk/don't-walk indicators for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

result.summary: The environment is a wide commercial corridor with faded pedestrian infrastructure and significant exposure to vehicle traffic. While sidewalks and signals are present, the large corner radii and lack of physical protection or traffic calming measures create a high-risk setting for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radii
hazards.description: The intersection design allows for high-speed vehicle turns, increasing the risk of collisions with pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right corners of the intersection

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street may block the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway near the white car

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to improve visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce crossing distance, slow turning vehicles, and improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, marked zebra crosswalks, and a traffic signal. However, safety is compromised by parked vehicles that obstruct sightlines at the crossing points and a lack of physical traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection obscure the view between pedestrians and drivers, increasing the risk of conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Curbside parking on both sides of the street approaching the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely degraded by active construction that completely blocks the right-side sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the roadway. On the left, narrow sidewalks are further obstructed by utility poles and parked vehicles, while faded crosswalk markings provide minimal protection at the crossing.

hazards.name: Construction Obstruction
hazards.description: Heavy machinery, traffic cones, and debris completely block the sidewalk on the right side of the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway and sidewalk area

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings are heavily worn and faded, reducing visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located in the center of the narrow left-side sidewalk, creating a barrier for mobility devices.

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Access Route
interventions.description: Establish a protected, ADA-compliant walkway around the construction zone using water-filled barriers or fencing.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental (ladder) markings to improve driver awareness.
